title: Architecture-aware kernel hub and adaptive prefill/decode pacing playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a small, centralized 'kernel hub' that maintains per-architecture and per-sequence-length kernel candidates and drives a low-cost runtime prober + adaptive pacing policy for prefill/decode phases. This ticket covers design, implementation, experiments, and rollout artifacts for a conservative production-first approach that minimizes latency tail regressions while improving avg tokens/sec and unit cost for mixed workloads. The hub should be lightweight, persist a compact fingerprint catalog, and surface a ranked set of kernel choices with confidence estimates. Complementary pacing logic will apply backpressure and reduce prefill/decode overlap in cases where KV/cache pressure or tail latency risk is detected.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel hub exists and exposes a JSON catalog of candidate kernels per arch/seqlen bucket
Runtime probes run in <50ms per probe and do not perturb request p95 by >2% in canary traffic
Adaptive prefill/decode pacing reduces tail-latency incidents (p99) on mixed prefill+decode workloads by >=15% in staging benchmarks
Telemetry events emitted for kernel choice decisions, probe results, and pacing triggers
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout path defined for canary -> regional -> global
Design doc and microbench results published to Confluence and PRs merged with tests and CI benchmarks
success_metrics: Avg tokens/sec improvement for T5-like workloads >= 6% on dedicated A100 pools
Unit cost reduction (inference GPU seconds) >= 5% for mixed-length chat traffic
p99 latency regression <= 1% on baseline steady-state traffic after rollout
False-positive pacing events (unnecessary throttles) < 0.5% of requests
technical_approach: Catalog: Build compact fingerprint key (arch, sm_version, seqlen_bucket, layout_hint) -> candidates with microbench stats (latency, throughput, memory) stored as protobuf-lite and a JSON view

Warmstart probing: Lightweight microprobe runner that executes representative mini-benchmarks on process start and periodically (low-QPS) to refresh stats; probes timeout at 30ms and are prioritized to avoid impacting production worker slots

Decision logic: Rank by constrained objective (latency SLO first, cost second) using an online score = latency_est * alpha + cost_est * beta with alpha tuned from ops SLOs; include confidence band to decide conservative/higher-throughput choices

Prefill/decode pacing: Token-level pacing policy that delays decode start for a short, adaptive window when memory/KV pressure or probe signals indicate elevated tail risk; uses token-budget quotas per request and global occupancy signals
Fallbacks: Multi-tier fallback chain (preferred-quantized, native, generic) with soft timeouts so requests can swap to fallback kernel without catastrophic failure
Observability: Add histograms for chosen_kernel, probe_latency_ms, pacing_action, prefill_decode_overlap_ms; integrate with existing per-route dashboards and cost breakdown
tradeoffs: Probing frequency vs. stability: more probes increase currency of catalog but can cause noisy measurements; we bias towards infrequent probes with strong statistical aggregation
Conservative defaults: to avoid p99 regressions we may forgo some throughput gains initially; acceptable given enterprise SLAs
In-process probing reduces cross-host variance but increases worker complexity; alternative is centralized probe service which adds network variance and rack-level shadowing complexity
Pacing increases tail safety at the expense of small avg-latency increases for a fraction of requests; we cap rate of pacing events and track customer-visible regressions
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Lab + microbench validation across 3 archs (NVIDIA A100, A10, AMD MI250) using synthetic and replay traffic
Phase 1: Staging canary on <1% production traffic with runtime flag enabled and strict kill-switch if p99 > baseline + 5%
Phase 2: Regional ramp to 10% with auto-rollforward if metrics stable for 24h, otherwise automatic rollback
Phase 3: Global rollout with route-level opt-outs for high-risk enterprise tenants until customer opt-in configured
Documentation and runbook published for on-call (how to disable hub, force kernel, inspect probe logs)
benchmarks_and_experiments: Microbench matrix: seqlen buckets [32,128,512,2048], batch sizes [1,4,16], archs [A100,A10,MI250], kernels [fused-attn,block-sparse,quantized-prefill]
Replay tests: 48h replay of production traffic from last 7 days with randomized kernel-hub decisions vs. baseline to estimate cost and latency impact
Shadow probe experiments: run probes in shadow mode for 1 week to collect distributional stats without affecting decisions
monitoring_and_alerting: SLO dashboards: p50/p95/p99 by route, with chosen_kernel breakdown
Alert: p99 delta > 3% for 15m -> page SRE and roll back runtime flag
Alert: probe success rate < 90% or probe_latency_ms median > 50ms -> automatic disable probing and notify infra
Cost signal: unit GPU-seconds increase > 7% sustained for 1h -> create ops task
